clue.text: Lloyd Webber musical mainly featuring naked floor show

indicators.note: featuring here means the shortened title has a word placed inside it
mainly means most of the word is kept, so the musical's title loses its final letter

parts.note: Cats is Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical about felines
naked means bare

explanation.surface: A newspaper listing for a stripped-down stage revival of a Lloyd Webber hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the musical's last letter, leaving CAT; 'featuring' means that shortened title holds the naked word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is entertainment staged in a nightclub or restaurant while the audience sits at tables, a classic floor show.

clue.text: You are soundly invested in a partner's lovers

indicators.note: invested in means put inside another word

parts.note: a mate is a partner, and 's adds S

indicators.note: soundly means the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: said aloud, you are gives the letters U R

explanation.surface: You are, it seems, financially tied up in a partner's affairs of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' says to hear the two words as letters; 'invested in' puts them inside. Lovers means enthusiasts who do something for love, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur, from the Latin for lover, does something for the love of it rather than pay.

clue.text: Growth of hypocrisy and end of faith in Australia

indicators.note: in means placed inside the Australia letters

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, pious talk

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of faith

explanation.surface: Hypocrisy and declining faith are spreading in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' looks like spreading, but it is a plant. 'end of' takes the last letter of faith; 'in' places both pieces within the country's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a plant, and a plant is a growth; its leaves inspired Corinthian column capitals.

clue.text: Initiative to go in with award for broadcast

parts.note: to enter is to go in

indicators.note: for broadcast means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a prize is an award

explanation.surface: A media firm shows initiative by entering a programme for a broadcasting award.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIZE and PRISE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is boldness and readiness to start new projects, which is initiative.

clue.text: Area south of Bear island

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means the letter is written below the bear word

parts.note: a cub is a young bear

explanation.surface: A map directs you to the region below Bear Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Sweet note found during blessing

indicators.note: found during means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a boon is a blessing
NB, nota bene, means note well

explanation.surface: A pleasant note heard during a church blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is not musical: it is the Latin nota bene. 'found during' places it inside the blessing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonbon is a small sweet or chocolate.

clue.text: Bore's degree of suitability

definitions.meaning: the ... of a gun is the diameter of its bore
quality or standard, how fit someone is

explanation.surface: Reads as a judgement on how fit a tedious person is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gun barrel's internal width and a person's quality or standard of ability.

clue.text: Moves to mate, perhaps willing to support objective

indicators.note: in a down clue to support means to sit beneath the other piece

parts.note: an end is an objective
game means willing, as in game for anything

explanation.surface: Suggests romantic advances to a partner, willing to back a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the endgame is the final phase, leading up to checkmate.

clue.text: Golf in Germany may need such a course

definitions.text: Golf in Germany may need such a course

parts.words: Golf in Germany may need such a course
parts.note: the Golf is a Volkswagen car, and a German car on a long drive needs a German motorway, not a golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer touring Germany wonders what sort of course to look for.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is the Volkswagen hatchback, and 'course' is a route, not a set of fairways.
explanation.definitionFit: The German motorway network is the route a car such as the Volkswagen would take on a fast journey.

clue.text: Game requiring select players to hold an ace

indicators.note: to hold means the casting word takes the next word inside it

parts.note: to cast a play is to select its players
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A sports report: a game where picked team members must keep hold of an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'select players' is a verb phrase, to choose actors; 'to hold' means that word takes the next word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played with two packs, so it is one example of a game.

clue.text: Feature of Porterhouse that's blemish on conspicuous wealth?

parts.note: to blemish something is to mar it
bling is slang for showy jewellery and flashy wealth

explanation.surface: A question whether Porterhouse, perhaps a Cambridge college, is a stain on ostentatious riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Porterhouse is a cut of beef, not a college; the fat streaks through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A good porterhouse steak shows streaks of fat running through the lean meat, which give it its look and flavour.

clue.text: Maiden horse surrounded by spooky group of creatures

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside the other word

parts.note: eerie means spooky
a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A girl's pony is encircled by ghostly animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' is not a girl but the cricket abbreviation; 'surrounded by' puts the horse inside the spooky word.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show.

clue.text: Line needed for bishop in improved communication

indicators.note: needed for means one character stands in place of another in the improved word

parts.note: improved means better
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman's message needs a better line, says the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed for' swaps the B of BETTER for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is a written message sent to someone, one standard form of communication.

clue.text: Pompous official judge's first with spirit after censure

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the censure word

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word judge is taken

parts.note: with means and, joining things together
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A self-important official is described: the judge leading the way, spirited after being reprimanded.
explanation.definitionFit: A panjandrum is a mock title for a self-important person who claims great authority.

clue.text: Butchers notoriously miss this change of direction in address

definitions.meaning: shop signs such as 'butchers' notoriously lack the punctuation mark showing possession
in rhetoric an ... is a turning aside to address someone absent

explanation.surface: Butchers miss a turn while giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a punctuation mark and a rhetorical device of turning to address someone.

clue.text: European woman seeing sharp practice curtailed?

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: sharp practice is dishonest dealing, fraud

explanation.surface: A woman from the Continent notices dishonest dealing being cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German title and word for a married woman, so a woman from Europe.

clue.text: Lad's holding fly that bites little bits

indicators.note: holding means one word goes round the other

parts.note: a lad is a son, and the 's gives the plural
a midge is a small biting fly

explanation.surface: Little bites from a fly that a boy has caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lad's' gives the plural of a boy word, and 'holding' wraps it round the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, so smidgeons are tiny bits.

clue.text: Bear has an obligation to the Queen

parts.note: should expresses obligation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A bear owes the monarch something.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to bear it.

clue.text: Accomplice must finish early, pinching antique Scottish pot

indicators.note: pinching means holding another piece inside
finish early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a crony is a close companion or accomplice
auld is Scots for old

explanation.surface: A partner in crime has to leave early, having stolen an old Scottish pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must finish early' drops the accomplice's last letter to leave CRON; 'pinching' makes that hold the Scots word, as in Auld Lang Syne.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large cooking pot.

clue.text: Go to the office, maybe work out after a change of heart

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letter is replaced by another

parts.note: to compute is to work out

explanation.surface: Someone decides to travel to work, perhaps after rethinking a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter P of COMPUTE becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: To commute is to travel regularly between home and work.

clue.text: Demanding way in which rowing crew will replace American

indicators.note: will replace means one piece takes the place of a letter

parts.note: taken as written
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A tough method where the rowers will stand in for an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighty means serious and burdensome, so demanding effort or attention.

clue.text: Feeling of pressure prime minister's limited?

indicators.note: limited means the name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Edward Heath was British prime minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A question whether a prime minister feels constrained under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To be under the heat is to be under pressure, as in 'the heat is on'.

clue.text: It's widely known duck enclosures on island last given precedence

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
pens are enclosures for animals

indicators.note: last given precedence means the final letter of the island is moved to the front

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A report of duck pens on an island, finally prioritised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last given precedence' moves the final E of CRETE to the front, making ECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is something supposedly confidential that everybody actually knows.

clue.text: Show great excitement as wife leaves cheat

indicators.note: leaves means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: a swizzle, or swizz, is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled as a spouse walks out on a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sizzle is to be full of excitement or passion, as hot fat crackles.

clue.text: Money requires care and attention after losing time

indicators.note: after losing means a letter is taken away

parts.note: to take trouble is to take care and attention

explanation.surface: Money needs looking after once the time has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency of Russia, so a unit of money.

clue.text: Arsenal weekly?

definitions.meaning: a store for arms and ammunition
a periodical, such as one published every week

explanation.surface: Reads like the name of a football club's weekly fanzine.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a store for weapons and a periodical publication.

clue.text: Take heart from new time of celebration

indicators.note: take heart from means the central letter is removed

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: Take courage from a new festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is Christmas, a season of celebration.

clue.text: Rests players at last after pride's shattered

indicators.note: after means the pick from players comes behind the rearranged letters
shattered means the letters are broken up and rearranged
at last means only the final letter of players is taken

explanation.surface: Players take a break after their pride is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' turns PRIDES into SPIDER. In snooker a spider is a raised rest for the cue.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a spider is a type of rest used to support the cue over a ball.

clue.text: Utterly destroyed and unlikely to have kicked about

indicators.note: to have, with about, means one word holds the other
about means surrounding the other word

parts.note: to toe something is to kick it
tall as in a tall story means unlikely

explanation.surface: Something wrecked and improbably kicked around.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlikely gives TALL via a tall story; 'to have ... about' means the kicked word goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalled is informal for wrecked beyond repair, as a car written off in a crash.

clue.text: Intense as lifebelt may be described

definitions.meaning: extremely intense, as of heat or pain
a lifebelt could be called a ..., a ring used at sea

explanation.surface: Reads as a lifeguard's description of how fierce a rescue was.
explanation.definitionFit: Searing heat or pain is extremely strong; the second reading splits the word as sea ring.
